study_info.title: Equivalent Switching Dose From Oral Risperidone to Risperidone Long-Acting Injection: A 48-Week Randomized, Prospective, Single-Blind Pharmacokinetic Study
study_info.authors: Ya Mei Bai, M.D., Ph.D.; Tzu Ting Chen, M.D.; Jen-Yeu Chen, M.D.; Wen-Ho Chang, M.D.; Bojian Wu, M.D.; Chih Hung Hung, M.D.; and Wen Kuo Lin, M.D.
study_info.study_design: 48-week, randomized, prospective, single-blind study; patients were randomly assigned to the oral risperidone group or the risperidone long-acting injection group. The method of randomization is not further specified.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Patients aged 18 to 65 years with DSM-IV diagnosis of schizophrenia, symptomatically stable (PANSS total score <80 at screening and baseline, each of the following PANSS parameters <4: conceptual disorganization, hallucinatory behavior, suspiciousness, unusual thought content), difference in CGI scores at screening and baseline <1, previous treatment with oral risperidone for at least 3 months prior to screening, otherwise good health based on physical exam, blood biochemistry, hematology, and medical history.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: History of neuroleptic malignant syndrome, documented organic disease of the central nervous system, or current seizure disorder; current risk of violent behavior against other individuals; current suicidal ideation or suicidal ideation during the 6 months preceding screening.
study_info.study_setting: Taiwan’s largest psychiatric teaching hospital, which offered long-term disposition for patients with poor social support, enabling stable patients to stay at the hospital for years.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Hospitalized patients at Taiwan’s largest psychiatric teaching hospital
study_info.dropout_reasons: One patient withheld informed consent due to gastrointestinal side effects at week 5, 2 patients were discharged in stable condition, and 2 patients taking 25 mg risperidone long-acting injection q 2 weeks (original oral risperidone doses of 3 mg/day and 4 mg/day, respectively) had symptom relapses.

minimal_units.intervention_details: Risperidone long-acting injection every 2 weeks: 25-mg injections for those receiving oral risperidone doses of 4 mg/day or less; 37.5-mg injections for those who had received oral risperidone at doses greater than 4 mg/day but at 6 mg/day or less; and 50-mg injections for those taking more than 6 mg/day of oral risperidone. Their original oral risperidone dose was maintained for the first 3 weeks, after which time it was either stopped or tapered off within 3 days.
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: Nurses administered and monitored all risperidone long-acting injections and oral medications throughout the course of the study to ensure drug compliance.
